scope: 15 final selector/API contracts; no scanner execution or universal case control

env.claim: Environment name lookup is case-sensitive on Unix-like systems and case-insensitive on Windows; values remain independent.

posix-env.claim: getenv searches the calling process environment; an unfound name returns null, distinct from a present empty value.

win-env.claim: The environment is process-scoped. GetEnvironmentStrings reads the caller environment, not every other process.

iis-appcmd.claim: AppCmd has separate object identifiers, configuration section paths and property/collection expressions.

iis-case.claim: IIS exposes IsCaseSensitive for individual property values; it is not a universal rule for identifiers or configuration syntax.

iis-attribute.claim: The documented MWA attribute-schema name indexer ignores case. This does not establish identical casing behavior for every AppCmd path component.

iis-config.claim: ApplicationHost configuration is schema-defined and extensible; section registrations and attributes identify configuration locations.

iis-section.claim: GetAdminSection resolves a named section at a path; an unsupported section returns ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND.

ps-case.claim: PowerShell command/parameter names and non-dictionary member access ignore case; modules can encounter filesystem exceptions, dictionaries can use other comparers.

ps-modules.claim: Module import can constrain a module by its name, GUID and version; a nullable constraint is not an invented module choice.

ps-select.claim: Select-Object selects named properties and can execute distinct selection options; property names must not be confused with arbitrary dictionary keys or values.

win-files.claim: Windows directories can have distinct case-sensitivity flags; effective path lookup is contextual, not globally insensitive.

win-paths.claim: Windows filename/path behavior also depends on filesystem and the API namespace in use.

sid.claim: EqualSid compares valid SID structures exactly; identity is not a generic case-folded account-name string.

sid-strings.claim: SID strings represent security identifiers; account display names and SDDL aliases are distinct representations.

sid-parse.claim: ConvertStringSidToSid parses a textual SID for the native API; parse failure is not proof that an account is absent.

account.claim: LookupAccountName resolves qualified names to SIDs in a target system/domain context; isolated names can be ambiguous.

registry.claim: Windows registry key names are case-insensitive; registry hierarchy is not a filesystem path namespace.

registry-value.claim: Registry value-name lookup is insensitive; a default value and key-level selection are distinct requests.

ntuser.claim: NTUSER.DAT is a user registry hive; accessing/loading profile hives is distinct from case comparison.

service.claim: SCM service names preserve spelling but compare case-insensitively; display names are not service keys.

rights.claim: Privilege constants identify specific Windows privileges; their documented macro spelling and API string are distinct.

account-rights.claim: Logon account rights use documented constants; account rights and privileges are related but not interchangeable sets.

wmi-path.claim: WMI object paths identify server/namespace/class/instance locations; a namespace is not a filesystem directory.

wmi-query.claim: Windows WMI WQL literal string data is case-insensitive, unlike the cited generic CIM rule.

wmi-grammar.claim: WQL has a grammar and typed comparisons; string relation tests are case-insensitive and invalid type/operator uses are errors.

wua.claim: Windows Update Search uses a criteria grammar with string comparisons insensitive unless specified; arbitrary SQL is not accepted.

wua-superseded.claim: The superseded-update option controls the candidate update population, not letter casing or collected-value comparison.

oval-windows.claim: Pinned source sid_object documents case-insensitive trustee names; Object fields and source behavior controls are preserved separately from native comparisons.

wmi-interface.claim: Windows WMI requires case-insensitive class names.

wmi-path-rules.claim: Windows WMI object-path comparisons are always case-insensitive.

native-acquisition.claim: Existing explicit filesystem/traversal and shared acquisition grammar; no new case setting or runtime default.

pid.rule: Numeric identity; letter case does not apply. Preserve declared integer/null meaning; do not stringify or invent a process.

positive.expectation: Select process identity 42 in the selected target context.

negative.expectation: A text operand is not an integer selector; no implicit conversion.

pid.uncertainty: No undocumented alias, Unicode folding, parser extension or provider behavior is assumed.

name.rule: Windows environment names compare insensitively; Unix-like environment names compare sensitively. A selected-process namespace and supplied platform must be known. Preserve bytes/spelling and values.

positive.expectation: Select PATH; Windows Path may also identify it.

negative.context: Unix target has PATH but not path
negative.expectation: No matching name; do not transplant Windows casing. Access failure is an error, not this absence.

name.uncertainty: No undocumented alias, Unicode folding, parser extension or provider behavior is assumed.

exceptions: Name lookup follows the target platform, not the scanner host or PowerShell wildcard behavior.
